title: Tech Note: Exchanging Data Between Processes

historical_commentary.text: This note tackles a perennial multi-process 4D application challenge: safely retrieving or setting values in another process's process variables, and keeping that communication synchronized rather than racing or deadlocking. Inter-process communication remains a real and relevant concern in current 4D applications, since 4D's classic multi-process model persists, though modern 4D offers additional tools (such as shared objects/collections and newer process-communication commands introduced well after 2004) that provide safer or more convenient alternatives to the manual process-variable techniques this note likely demonstrated.
related_updates: Later 4D versions introduced shared objects and shared collections (with built-in synchronization) as safer alternatives to manual process-variable exchange for many use cases
4D's process communication command set has been expanded since 2004 with additional options for inter-process messaging
The fundamental need to synchronize communication between concurrent processes remains unchanged and is still a core multi-process programming concern
